summary: Fine-tuning makes sense when you need to change a model's behavior, style, or format consistently, teach it a specialized domain vocabulary, or improve reliability on narrow tasks that prompting alone can't stabilize. Use RAG when the problem is access to fresh or proprietary knowledge, and prompt engineering when you can get acceptable results by steering a capable base model. In 2026, investment and adoption are consolidating around platform and infrastructure layers (LLM gateways, agent ops, and managed fine-tuning), with open-source frameworks like Axolotl, LLaMA-Factory, and Unsloth dominating self-hosted workflows.
when_to_fine_tune: Choose fine-tuning when you need consistent output format, tone, or structured behavior that prompting cannot reliably enforce at scale.
Fine-tune for domain adaptation when the model must internalize specialized vocabulary or reasoning patterns not present in its base training.
Prefer RAG over fine-tuning when your core need is injecting fresh, frequently-changing, or proprietary factual knowledge.
Fine-tune to reduce latency and token cost by baking in instructions, letting you use shorter prompts and smaller models in production.
